**CAPSTONE PROJECT ABSTRACT**

Title: **ORDINEX: A Mobile-Based Municipal Ordinance Reporting and Monitoring System for Bacnotan, La Union**

Researchers:

**Almodovar, Mark Allen C.**

**Quimson, Jibreel A.**

**Rivera, Glenn N.**

**Roldan, Jan Alexis G.**

Type of Document: **CAPSTONE PROJECT**

Type of Publication: Unpublished

Accrediting Institution: Lorma Colleges

    CLI Bldg, Urbiztondo, San Juan, La Union

Teacher-In-Charge: **Shekiro R. Raposas, MTS, MIS**

**ABSTRACT**

*Municipal ordinance violations in Bacnotan, La Union were reported mostly through verbal reports at the barangay hall and sent to several different offices. Residents hesitated to report because of privacy concerns, and many who did report were only sometimes informed of what happened to their reports.*

*ORDINEX was developed as a mobile-based municipal ordinance reporting and monitoring system that allowed residents to submit reports with descriptions, photos, and location tags and to follow the status of their reports in real time, and that gave municipal administrators a web-based administrator panel to review reports, update statuses, and monitor violations. The system was built with Flutter and Dart for the android application, React for the admin panel, and Firebase for authentication, database, and cloud storage, following the Kanban methodology. It was evaluated through a needs survey of 40 respondents and a usability evaluation by 45 respondents using the System Usability Scale (SUS).*

*The findings showed that privacy concern was the leading reason for not reporting (59.5%) and that 82.5% of the respondents were inclined to use a mobile reporting application. ORDINEX obtained a mean SUS score of 82.11, which was rated Good and above the target score of 70\. The system contributed to more accessible, traceable, and organized reporting of municipal ordinance violations.*

**Keywords:** *Ordinance Reporting, Municipal Ordinance Monitoring, Mobile Application, E-Governance, Local Government*

**Chapter I**

**INTRODUCTION**

This chapter presented the project context, conceptual framework, statement of objectives, scope and limitations of the study, purpose and description, and technical background of the proposed system. 

**Project Context**

International studies emphasized the importance of digital transformation and automated reporting systems in improving public service delivery and governance. Research in Information Systems showed that organizations adopting digital technologies experienced improved operational efficiency, enhanced communication, and better data management.

Wang, W., Zhu, G., and Mo, S. (2024) explained that digital transformation improved organizational monitoring and strengthened compliance management through efficient information systems. Their study highlighted that digital platforms supported accountability and improved governance processes.

Similarly, Muhammad-Bello, B. K. et al. (2022) developed iReportNow, a mobile-based reporting system that enabled users to submit reports digitally using mobile devices. The study revealed that digital reporting platforms improved accessibility, reduced delays in communication, and strengthened 

coordination between citizens and authorities.

In another international study, Fadess, G. et al. (2024) developed a mobile-based reporting and handling application for public service operations. The study emphasized that integrating mobile technologies, location tracking, and real-time communication improved monitoring processes and allowed authorities to respond more effectively to community concerns.

Studies on digital public service platforms also showed that automated communication systems improved accessibility and responsiveness in government services. 

Furthermore, Kalaba, C. J. (2023) stated that data-driven systems enhanced the capability of local governments to make informed decisions through real-time access to organized data. Likewise, Sayogo, D. S. et al. (2023) emphasized that digital data management systems improved transparency and operational monitoring in government institutions.

These international studies supported the development of the proposed ordinance reporting system by demonstrating how digital reporting platforms, centralized databases, and real-time monitoring improved governance, accessibility, efficiency, and public service delivery.

In the Philippines, several studies highlighted the growing adoption of digital technologies and e-governance systems to improve local government services and communication with citizens.

Jakaria, S. (2025) discussed the digital transformation challenges and opportunities in the Philippines. The study explained that while digitalization improved governance efficiency, successful implementation depended on system accessibility, usability, and proper technological integration.

In a study conducted in Zamboanga City, Barrios, N. A. and Moreno, F. (2024) evaluated e-government initiatives and found that digital government platforms improved transparency, service accessibility, and communication between citizens and local governments.

Additionally, Castilla, R. et al. (2023) emphasized that mobile government applications improved public access to government information and services. The study showed that web and mobile technologies increased citizen participation and improved the dissemination of public information.

Meanwhile, Desmal, A. J. et al. (2022) concluded that usability, accessibility, and responsiveness were important factors affecting user acceptance and satisfaction in mobile government services.

These national studies supported the proposed ordinance reporting system by demonstrating that web-based government platforms and digital reporting systems improved communication, accessibility, transparency, and operational efficiency in Philippine local governance.

Local studies related to barangay and municipal information systems further supported the development of a web-based ordinance reporting and monitoring platform.

Mando, R. (2022) developed a Barangay E-Complaint Management System designed to improve the organization and monitoring of community complaints. The study revealed that digital complaint systems reduced delays, improved data organization, and strengthened communication between residents and barangay officials.

Similarly, Ormillo, J. M. et al. (2026) introduced e-BOMIS, a web-based barangay management system that digitalized community services and records management. Their findings showed that centralized web systems improved operational efficiency, record accessibility, and data management in barangay operations.

Engbino, K. A. et al. (2024) developed a web-based monitoring system for barangay projects integrated with SMS and email notification features. The researchers found that real-time notifications improved responsiveness and kept stakeholders informed about updates and activities.

Another local study by Bautista, M. T. et al. (2023) introduced BALANGAY, a Mobile-Based document request and reporting system with decision support features for barangay program development. The study emphasized that digital platforms improved reporting efficiency, information accessibility, and decision-making within local government units.

Furthermore, Rivas, R. M. (2026) developed a Barangay Information Management System integrated with automated mobile messaging to enhance community engagement. The study demonstrated that automated communication systems improved information dissemination and strengthened interaction between local governments and residents.

In another local study, Nerona, G. et al. (2026) explored the improvement of data management systems in a local government unit in Baguio City through information system solutions. The researchers concluded that centralized digital systems enhanced sustainable public service delivery by improving data organization, operational efficiency, and accessibility of government records.

Lastly, Adarle, L. J. et al. (2025) developed DrivePal using geofencing technology. The study highlighted that integrating location-based technologies improved monitoring accuracy and supported faster reporting and response processes.

These local studies supported the proposed ordinance reporting and monitoring system by demonstrating the effectiveness of web-based reporting platforms, centralized databases, notification systems, and real-time monitoring solutions in improving local governance and community engagement. 

## **Conceptual Framework**

![][image3]

**Figure 1**. Conceptual Framework (Mobile Application)

This figure illustrated the conceptual framework of the Mobile-Based Municipal Ordinance Reporting and Monitoring System, which followed the Input–Process–Output (IPO) model. The input included user-provided data such as report descriptions, images, location coordinates, and municipal ordinance information. The process included data submission through the Mobile application, validation and storage in Firebase, real-time processing of reports, and notification to local government officials. These components worked together to collect, organize, and manage report data efficiently. The output consisted of organized reports, real-time notifications, accessible ordinance information, and improved monitoring of violations. This framework highlighted the system’s capability to provide a structured, efficient, and user-friendly reporting experience that enhanced communication and supported better decision-making in the municipality.

**Statement of Objectives**    

This study achieved to design and develop a Mobile-Based Municipal Ordinance Reporting and Monitoring System for Bacnotan, La Union that improved the accessibility, efficiency, and organization of reporting ordinance violations in Bacnotan, La Union.

Specifically, the study sought to:

1. To identify the common challenges encountered by residents and local government units in reporting and managing municipal ordinance violations;  
2. To design and develop a Mobile-Based Municipal Ordinance Reporting and Monitoring System for Bacnotan, La Union that allowed users to submit reports using text, images, and location data; and  
3. To evaluate the usability and effectiveness of the developed system using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and user feedback from selected respondents.

**Scope and Limitation of the Study**

This study focused on the design and development of a mobile-based application that enabled residents of Bacnotan, La Union to report and monitor municipal ordinance violations. The system allowed users to submit reports through internet-based access using text input, image capture, and location tagging to provide accurate and detailed information. All submitted reports were stored in a centralized database, which could be accessed by local government officials for monitoring, tracking, and managing reports. 

However, the study had several limitations. The system relied on internet connectivity, which might affect accessibility and performance for users with weak or unstable network connections. The accuracy and reliability of submitted reports depended on the information provided by users, which might occasionally be incomplete, inaccurate, or insufficient for verification purposes. In addition, the system was tested only among selected respondents and within specific areas in Bacnotan, La Union; therefore, the findings might not fully represent the experiences and conditions of the entire municipality. The proposed system was intended solely as a support tool for reporting and monitoring municipal ordinance violations and was not designed to replace official law enforcement procedures or decision-making processes. Furthermore, advanced functionalities such as integration with national government systems, and cross-platform compatibility for all mobile operating systems were not included in the current version of the application. At the time of the study, the mobile implementation and optimization of the system were limited to iOS Apple devices only. 

**Purpose and Description** 

The primary purpose of this study was to design and develop ORDINEX: A Mobile-Based Municipal Ordinance Reporting and Monitoring System for Bacnotan, La Union to improve the efficiency, accessibility, and organization of reporting municipal ordinance violations in the Municipality of Bacnotan, La Union. The proposed system aimed to address the limitations of traditional reporting methods such as verbal complaints, written reports, and social media postings, which often resulted in delayed responses, unorganized records, and communication gaps between residents and local government units (LGUs). Consistent with studies emphasizing the importance of digital transformation in local governance, the system sought to provide a centralized and technology-driven platform that supported faster communication, improved monitoring, and more efficient public service delivery.

ORDINEX was designed as a Mobile-based reporting and monitoring platform that enabled residents to submit ordinance violation reports using text descriptions, image attachments, GPS location data, and timestamps through their mobile devices. The system utilized Firebase as a cloud-based backend for secure data storage, authentication, and real-time synchronization of reports and updates. Through centralized database management, local government officials could efficiently monitor, verify, organize, and respond to report in real time. 

The proposed system was expected to benefit several stakeholder groups. For residents, the platform provided a convenient and accessible means of reporting violations without the need for physical visits or manual paperwork. It ensured that submitted concerns were properly documented, monitored, and addressed by authorities. For local government personnel, the system supported efficient report management, real-time monitoring, faster response times, and improved decision-making through centralized access to information. The community also benefited from improved transparency, accountability, and awareness of municipal ordinances, contributing to a safer and more organized environment.

Furthermore, the study provided the researchers with practical experience in system development, cloud computing, Mobile technologies, while addressing a real-world governance problem. The project might also serve as a reference for future researchers interested in e-governance systems, intelligent reporting platforms. Overall, ORDINEX aimed to support a more responsive, technology-driven, and citizen-centered local governance system through the integration of modern Mobile technologies.

**Technical Background**

**Figma**. A software designed for designing and prototyping, they used Figma to plan how they wanted the system to look and plan out the layout and design of the system. It enabled the researchers to have a visual design of the different screens and the navigation of the design of the system before it was built.

**Flutter.** Framework used to build the mobile app for the system. Flutter was used to help developers in making the mobile app visually appealing and smooth on the Android mobile phones. Also, a single codebase can be used to develop apps for multiple platforms.

**Dart.** Dart was the language that was used in the Flutter based mobile app. It was the programming language of choice for developers to develop the features of the app, run the app and develop the user interface.

**React.** The React JS Library for developing the Web-based Admin Panel. This library allowed creating a responsive and interactive interface that allowed an administrator to manage reports and access the necessary information about the system quickly.

It contained some features such as Reusable Components that made developing and maintaining the system easier.

**Firebase.** It was a cloud-based platform that the researchers chose to use for storing, managing, and organizing the data. Firebase managed all of the user’s information, their submitted reports, uploaded image(s), status of reported issue(s) along with their timestamps.

Firebase also allowed the researchers to use many useful services such as real-time database updates, Cloud Storage, User Authentication, etc., which kept both the mobile application and Admin Panel connected to each other and always able to get updated info from the Firebase database.

**Cloud-Based System**. was a system that help its data and applications in remote servers instead of restricting it to local devices. In this research, Firebase acted as the cloud-based technology, which provided users and administrators with access to data through the app and through the web-based admin panel.

**Cross-Platform**. The term indicated that an application was usable on different operating systems with a single codebase. The capability was provided by Flutter in the research presented in the current work, where the Android platform is used as the mobile application’s target.

**System Elements**

**Mobile Application**. The element of the system meant for residents reporting relevant problems relating to municipal regulations. Through the application, the users were able to make reports, take pictures with their cameras, provide information about a location, and follow their problems’ statuses.

**Web-Based Admin Panel**. This was a platform that was web-based and was utilized by local government administrators who had the relevant authority. At this accessible platform, administrators were able to approve the reports that the residents made. They also had the ability to confirm complaints, access images uploaded by residents, update statuses of submitted complaints, and also respond to residents’ inquiries. Any change made was instantly reflected in the mobile application.

**Authentication**. The service used for authentication was called Firebase. It was a service that helped in verification of the identity of the residents and the administrators before they gained access to the system.

**Cloud Storage**. A Firebase service allowed secure storage of images provided by citizens to support their reports. Every image uploaded linked back to the corresponding report, so administrators could easily check the submitted complaints.

**System Specifications**

**Image Capture and Data Privacy Policy.** A feature which allowed residents to take photos and upload them as supporting evidence for their report. The system showed a notice of data privacy before an image is uploaded, alerting users that the images they took might contain personal/sensitive information, so that people would be aware of how the uploaded pictures would be collected, stored and used.

**Timestamping (Date and Time Logging)**. A functionality that automatically notes down the exact date and time when a report is submitted or when an image or picture is uploaded or captured. This information remains stored along with the report providing information as to when the report was created. It also enables the administrators to keep track of action taken on the report in a timely manner.

**Real-Time Monitoring and Tracking of Application Status**. This functionality gaves an opportunity to the residents to get acquainted with the process of their submitted reports any time. Changes made to the reports were automatically seen in the application without the need for manually refreshing the page.

**Report Status.** referred to the current progression of the concern that a resident had submitted via the system. Every report had its own unique status to allow residents and administrators to keep track of whether or not their concerns have been addressed.

**Pending** – This meant that the report had been successfully submitted, but had yet to be looked at and worked on by the administrators.

**Ongoing** – the administrators had already seen the report and were looking into addressing the concern right now.

**Completed** \- Indicated that the reported issue was now resolved or that the administrator had performed what was needed.

### **General Terms**

**User Interface (UI)**. The look and feel of the system and the way the system interacted with users through screens, buttons, menus and other controls. It was the primary method by which users reported incidents and explored and accessed the various components of the application.

**UX (User Experience)**. Was the overall experience that a user had when using the system. It involved the application being simple and easily navigated, user-friendly, intuitive, simple to operate, and easy to understand.

**CHAPTER II**

**DESIGN AND METHODOLOGY**

In this chapter, the researchers presented the framework used in the development and evaluation of the Mobile-Based Municipal Ordinance Reporting and Monitoring System. It discussed the research design, research population and locale, ethical considerations, data gathering tools and procedures, and the software development methodology used in this study.

**Research Design**    

	Using a mixed-methods approach to collect both quantitative and qualitative data produced a new research validation of the usability, functionality, and effectiveness of the system. This type of study allowed researchers to evaluate the system using both technical criteria and user criteria.

Quantitative data were collected by means of structured questionnaires, mainly from usability evaluation toolkits . These tools allowed researchers to evaluate ease of use, system performance, and user satisfaction. Researchers could use these data points as measurable outcomes of the system's ability to process reports and provide information effectively and efficiently.

To get qualitative data the researchers used interviews and also conducted feedback meetings with a sample of users. Through this process the researchers gained a wealth of qualitative information about user expectations, common problems when filing ordinance violation reports, user attitude and preference about the proposed system.

With the two forms of data analyzed together, the researchers were able to conduct a thorough analysis of the system, including usability, system performance and projected success in the real world.

**Population and Locale**

The study was conducted in selected areas within the Municipality of Bacnotan, La Union, Philippines. Instead of covering the entire municipality, the research focused only on chosen barangays where the implementation and testing of the proposed system were feasible. 

These respondents were chosen because they were directly involved in reporting, managing, and maintaining the system for municipal ordinance violations and were likely to benefit from a digital reporting and monitoring system. Purposive sampling was used to select participants, ensuring that the respondents were relevant to the objectives of the study and capable of providing meaningful feedback.

**Ethical Considerations** 

This study adhered to ethical standards to ensure the protection of the rights and welfare of all individuals involved in the development and evaluation of the system. The researchers utilized standardized data gathering instruments such as letters, questionnaires, surveys, and interviews (see Appendix A, B, and C) to collect relevant data from respondents aligned with the objectives of the study. All research activities were carried out in accordance with established ethical principles governing academic research and information technology development, and every measure was taken to safeguard participant welfare throughout the entire research process. The ethical considerations observed in this study covered six key areas: informed consent, voluntary participation, confidentiality, data privacy protection, proper use of data, and system security measures.

Prior to data collection, the researchers provided a clear and understandable explanation of the study to obtain informed consent from all participants. Respondents were informed about the purpose, scope, procedures, and evaluation process of the research before agreeing to participate. They were given the opportunity to ask questions and seek clarification at any point in the process, and a written explanation of how their data would be utilized was made available to them. Participation in the study was entirely voluntary. Respondents were explicitly informed that they were free to refuse or withdraw from the study at any time without any form of penalty, pressure, or negative consequence. No participant was coerced or obligated to take part, and the researchers ensured that this principle was upheld throughout all phases of data collection. The study was conducted in a secure and controlled environment to ensure that data gathering was carried out properly and ethically at all times.

The confidentiality and privacy of all participants were strictly maintained throughout the conduct of the study. The identities of respondents were not disclosed in any part of the manuscript, and all responses were reported in aggregated or summary form only. No personally identifiable information such as names, contact details, or individual answers was included in the appendices, results, or discussion sections of this research. All collected data were used solely for academic and research purposes and were not shared with any unauthorized individuals or third parties. Data files containing respondent information were stored securely in password-protected digital storage accessible only to the researchers directly involved in the study. The data collected were handled with the highest level of care and would be disposed of responsibly upon the completion of the study.

With respect to data privacy compliance, the development and operation of ORDINEX did not violate the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173\) of the Philippines, as long as all data collected through the system were responsibly managed and were not disclosed or made accessible to the general public or to any unauthorized parties. The system was designed so that all submitted ordinance violation reports  including attached images, GPS location coordinates, timestamps, and any personal information provided by reporting users were stored exclusively within a secured Firebase cloud database with strictly restricted access controls. Only duly authorized municipal personnel and the designated system administrators were permitted to view, process, and act upon the submitted reports. No data collected or generated by the system was made publicly accessible, published, or distributed in any form without the explicit authorization of the appropriate municipal authorities. It was important to emphasize that the potential violation of RA 10173 arose only when personal data was disclosed to unauthorized individuals or released to the public without the knowledge and consent of the data subjects. So long as ORDINEX operated within its controlled-access environment where data remained confined to authorized users and was used exclusively for the legitimate purpose of ordinance violation monitoring the system fully upheld the core principles of the Data Privacy Act of 2012, namely transparency, legitimate purpose, and proportionality. The researchers ensured that data privacy was treated as a fundamental design requirement of ORDINEX, not merely a compliance formality, thereby making the system a legally sound and responsible platform for local government use.

Finally, the ORDINEX system incorporated robust technical safeguards to protect all user data and system-generated information from unauthorized access, further reinforcing its compliance with RA 10173\. The system implemented secure user authentication through Firebase Authentication, requiring registered accounts and verified credentials before any report could be submitted or accessed. Role-based access control was applied to ensure that municipal administrators and registered residents operated strictly within their designated permission levels, preventing unauthorized viewing or manipulation of sensitive report data. Input validation and error handling mechanisms were integrated to prevent malicious data entry and maintain the integrity of the reporting database. Access to raw data was restricted exclusively to the researchers and authorized municipal personnel, and no report content was exposed to any external or public-facing interface. These system-level security measures collectively demonstrated the researchers’ commitment to responsible and ethical technology development, ensuring that ORDINEX functioned as a trustworthy, legally compliant, and privacy-respecting digital governance platform for the Municipality of Bacnotan, La Union.

**Data Gathering Tools and Procedure** 

	This study employed multiple data gathering instruments to collect both qualitative and quantitative data needed for the development and evaluation of ORDINEX. The instruments used were an interview guide, a structured survey questionnaire(see appendix b) grounded on the System Usability Scale (SUS)(see appendix c). Each instrument served a specific purpose aligned with the objectives of the study.

      	An interview guide was used to gather information regarding the current system and operational challenges faced by the municipality of Bacnotan, La Union. The questions were designed to elicit responses about existing workflows, system limitations, and the specific features desired by stakeholders, including municipal staff and residents, for the proposed ORDINEX system. The interview guide facilitated the identification of common challenges in ordinance violation reporting, which served as the foundation for the system’s functional requirements.

      	The System Usability Scale (SUS) questionnaire was employed to specifically measure the usability and user satisfaction of the application, providing a standardized and quantifiable assessment of how effectively and efficiently users could interact with the system.

      	Both evaluation instruments employed a 5-point Likert scale to measure respondents’ level of agreement with each item, ranging from 1 (Strongly Disagree) to 5 (Strongly Agree). This scale enabled the researchers to quantify subjective user opinions into measurable numerical data that could be statistically analyzed. The survey responses and the ORDINEX-specific statements were analyzed using the Weighted Mean formula, while the SUS responses were scored using the standard SUS formula described under Data Analysis. 

**Procedure**

      	The data gathering procedure followed a systematic and chronological process, from securing the necessary approvals through to the final analysis of collected data. The following steps were carried out by the researchers.

      	First, the researchers prepared and submitted a formal letter of request to the Municipality of Bacnotan, La Union, stating the purpose and scope of the study. Upon receipt of the letter, the management reviewed and granted approval, authorizing the researchers to proceed with data collection activities. The researchers then coordinated with designated municipal personnel to schedule interviews, identify respondents, and establish guidelines for the conduct of the study.

      	Second, the researchers conducted structured interviews with key stakeholders, including the office manager and relevant municipal staff responsible for managing ordinance violation reports. The interview aimed to identify operational challenges, document existing workflows, and capture the specific functional requirements for the ORDINEX system. The responses gathered were analyzed to extract user expectations, system constraints, and key features that would guide the design and development of the application.

      	Third, the gathered requirements were translated into system features, functionalities, and user interface designs. The development team implemented the core modules of ORDINEX, including the report submission module, GPS location tagging, image capture, and real-time monitoring dashboard. The developed system underwent rigorous functional and usability testing to identify and resolve bugs, errors, and performance issues prior to its deployment for user evaluation.

      	Fourth, the survey questionnaire and SUS instrument were distributed(see appendix c) to a total of 45 respondents, composed of 20 residents, 10 barangay staff, 8 municipal staff, 2 national agency personnel, and 5 technical support personnel from selected barangays within Bacnotan, La Union. The questionnaires were administered through Google Forms during the evaluation period. Respondents were given ample time to interact with the system before completing the evaluation forms to ensure that their feedback accurately reflected their experience with ORDINEX. 

      	

### **Data Analysis**

The responses to the needs survey and to the ORDINEX-specific statements were analyzed using the Weighted Mean, which was the sum of the products of each rating and its frequency divided by the number of respondents. The weighted means were interpreted using the following scale: 4.21 to 5.00 Strongly Agree, 3.41 to 4.20 Agree, 2.61 to 3.40 Neutral, 1.81 to 2.60 Disagree, and 1.00 to 1.80 Strongly Disagree.

The responses to the ten SUS statements were scored using the standard SUS formula and not the Weighted Mean. For each odd numbered statement (items 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9), the contribution was the rating minus 1\. For each even numbered statement (items 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10), the contribution was 5 minus the rating. The ten contributions were added and multiplied by 2.5, which gave an SUS score from 0 to 100 for each respondent. In formula form, SUS \= 2.5 × \[Σ(rating − 1 for odd items) \+ Σ(5 − rating for even items)\]. The overall SUS score was the mean of the individual SUS scores, and it was interpreted using the rating scale in Figure 2, with 70 as the target score.

| SUS Score Range  | Category  | Interpretation  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Below 60  | Poor  | Indicates low usability; system needs major improvements  |
| 60 – 69  | Marginal  | Indicates low usability; system needs major improvements  |
| 70 – 79  | Marginal  | Meets minimum usability standards  |
| 70 – 79  | Good  | High usability and user satisfaction |
| 90 – 100  | Excellent  | Very high usability and system performance  |

**Figure 2**. System Usability Scale (SUS) Score Interpretation

Figure 2 illustrated the interpretation of the System Usability Scale (SUS) scores used to evaluate the usability of the proposed system. The SUS score ranged from 0 to 100 and was categorized into different levels: Poor (below 60), Marginal (60–69), Acceptable (70–79), Good (80–89), and Excellent (90–100). Higher scores indicated better usability, user satisfaction, and system performance, while lower scores suggested the need for improvements. This scale served as a standardized tool to assess how effectively and efficiently users could interact with the system.

**Software Methodology**

**![][image4]**

**Figure 3\.** Kanban

The development of the ORDINEX: A Mobile-Based Municipal Ordinance Reporting and Monitoring System for Bacnotan, La Union followed the Kanban Software Development Methodology. This methodology was selected because the project required continuous development, testing, monitoring, and improvement of multiple interconnected system components such as ordinance reporting, geolocation services, image uploading, cloud-based storage, and real-time notifications. Unlike traditional software development models that followed a fixed and sequential process, Kanban provided a flexible and continuous workflow that allowed developers to manage tasks efficiently while continuously improving the system throughout the development cycle.

To implement the methodology, the researchers utilized a Kanban board to visually organize and monitor the progress of tasks during system development. The Kanban board was divided into workflow columns namely Backlog, Requirements, Design, Development, Testing, Deployment, and Done or Review. Each feature and development activity was represented as a task card that moved across the board depending on its progress. This process allowed the researchers to monitor workflow efficiently, identify delays, manage priorities, and maintain productivity during development.

In the Backlog Phase, the researchers identified and organized all planned system features and development tasks. The researchers reviewed related literature, analyzed existing ordinance reporting problems, and listed the core functionalities required for the proposed system. The backlog included features such as report submission using text, images, and location data, real-time report monitoring, notification systems, user authentication, and centralized database management. These tasks were divided into smaller and manageable activities to simplify implementation and monitoring.

During the **Requirements Phase**, the researchers conducted surveys, interviews, and consultations with selected residents and municipal staff within Bacnotan, La Union. The purpose of this phase was to identify the common issues encountered in traditional ordinance reporting systems and determine the needs of both residents and local government personnel. Based on the collected information, the researchers defined the system requirements including the need for accessible Mobile-based reporting, real-time updates, efficient monitoring tools.

In the **Development Phase,** researchers carried out the actual coding and implementation of the features of the system. Kanban approach meant that tasks were continually picked and incrementally implemented. The Android application was built using Flutter and Dart, and the web-based admin panel was built using React.js. Firebase was the cloud-based backend and database management system to store and manage user information, submitted reports, uploaded image records, report statuses, timestamps and other system data.

At this stage of the project, researchers developed the submission module, the image capture and upload feature, the ability to manually enter locations, the automatic recording of the date and time, the ability to monitor reports in real-time, the ability to receive notifications and an administrative monitoring dashboard. Researchers also developed a notification indicating that sensitive/personal information could be included with uploaded images after image upload.

Researchers also integrated APIs between the mobile app and the web-based admin panel, the Firebase platform.

During the **Testing Phase**, assessment was carried out on all modules and features to identify and fix bugs as a means of verifying that they all worked as intended. Functional assessments were completed to ensure that submitted reports’ accuracy, uploaded images, manually input locations, corrected timestamps, updated status in real time, and delivered notifications all worked correctly. Testing was also done on novel database synchronization and system response times to see if any changes made by Admins were reflected in real time on users’ mobile applications. In addition, an assessment was completed via usability testing for selected respondents to determine how easy it was to use the system, how accessible the system was, how responsive each function was, and how well the entire system performed as a working product. Selected respondents completed a System Usability Scale (SUS) questionnaire to provide feedback regarding their experiences and measure the usability of the application developed.   
During the **Deployment Phase**, the completed system was deployed and made accessible to selected users within the municipality. Final integration and debugging were conducted to ensure that all components operated properly in the live environment. The researchers also prepared the system for presentation, demonstration, and evaluation.

The completed system was installed and made available to selected users within the municipality. Finally the integration, debugging and database settings were done to ensure that all the components were working fine in the live environment. The researchers also prepared the system for presentation, demonstration and evaluation.

Finally, in the Done or **Review Phase**, the researchers evaluated the overall effectiveness, reliability, and usability of the developed system. The researchers analyzed the results of the usability evaluation, user feedback, and system performance to determine whether the objectives of the study were successfully achieved. Identified issues and recommendations for improvement were documented to support future enhancements of the system. The review phase also provided insights for future development such as expanding reporting features, and integrating additional technologies for more efficient municipal ordinance monitoring.

**Table 2\. Kanban Workflow Phases and Deliverables**

| Phase | Key Tasks | Deliverable |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Backlog | Identify ordinance reporting issues, review related literature, and list planned system features | Prioritized feature list |
| Requirements | Conduct surveys and interviews to identify system requirements and user needs | System requirement specifications |
| Design | Create interface layouts, database structure, workflows, and system architecture | Wireframes and system design |
| Development | Develop frontend interface, integrate Firebase services | Functional Mobile-based application |
| Testing | Conduct functional testing, usability testing, and SUS evaluation | Testing reports and SUS results |
| Deployment | Deploy the system and perform final integration and debugging | Operational Mobile-based system |
| Done/Review | Evaluate system performance, analyze user feedback, and identify future improvements | Final evaluation and recommendations |

**CHAPTER III**

**RESULTS AND DISCUSSION**

This chapter presented the results obtained from the data gathering and evaluation conducted for the development of ORDINEX: A Mobile-Based Municipal Ordinance Reporting and Monitoring System for Bacnotan, La Union. It discussed the findings based on the objectives of the study. Specifically, this chapter presented the common challenges encountered by residents and municipal personnel in reporting ordinance violations, the implementation of the developed system, and the usability evaluation conducted using the System Usability Scale (SUS). The results were presented using tables, figures, and descriptive discussions to provide a comprehensive interpretation of the collected data 

**Common Challenges Encountered by Residents and Local Government Units in Reporting and Managing Municipal Ordinance Violations**

The first objective of the study was to identify the common challenges encountered by residents and local government units in reporting and managing municipal ordinance violations. To achieve this, the researchers gathered the experiences and opinions of forty (40) respondents from selected barangays of Bacnotan, La Union using the survey questionnaire. These were the residents, barangay staff, municipal staff, and national agency personnel listed in Table 1 of Chapter II; the five technical support personnel in that table took part only in the system evaluation. The results covered the respondents’ profile, their reporting experience, the reasons for not reporting, the response they received, their perceptions of the current process, and their expectations of a mobile reporting application.

This suggests a need for a more accessible and convenient reporting mechanism, such as ORDINEX, to encourage consistent reporting and improve the monitoring of ordinance violations.

Eight respondents (20.0%) had not reported. Reports were sent mostly to barangay officials (75.0%), then to the municipal office (50.0%), the police (42.5%), and the social media page of the LGU (30.0%). Because respondents could choose more than one answer, a single violation might reach several offices through face-to-face or informal channels, leaving no single organized record. Table 6 revealed that the leading barrier to reporting was concern about the privacy of information (22 respondents, 55.0%). It was followed by fear of retaliation or conflict (27.5%), too much time or effort (27.5%), not knowing where or how to report (22.5%), and not believing that action would be taken (15.0%). Of the 40 respondents, 2 left the question blank and 1 answered that he or she had not witnessed any violation. Some respondents who answered had also reported at least once, so the table showed the barriers that respondents perceived and not only the reasons of those who never reported. When only the 12 respondents who witnessed a violation and did not report at least once were counted, privacy concern was still the most common reason (9 respondents, 75.0%). This meant that confidentiality was a bigger barrier to reporting than the effort involved, and that fear of being identified discouraged residents from reporting.

**Design and Development of ORDINEX: A Mobile-Based Municipal Ordinance Reporting and Monitoring System**

This section presented the developed Mobile-Based Municipal Ordinance Reporting and Monitoring System (ORDINEX). The system was designed and developed based on the challenges identified during the data gathering phase. The primary objective of the system was to provide residents of Bacnotan, La Union with an accessible platform for reporting municipal ordinance violations while enabling municipal personnel to efficiently monitor, verify, and manage submitted reports.

The development of the system followed the Kanban software development methodology. Flutter and Dart were used in developing the mobile application, React was utilized for the web-based administrative panel, and Firebase served as the cloud-based backend for authentication, database management, and real-time synchronization.

**Figure 4**

**User Login Interface**

![][image5]

Figure 4 showed the login interface of ORDINEX. The login page allowed registered users to securely access the application using their authorized credentials. Firebase Authentication validated user accounts before granting access to the system.

This authentication mechanism ensured that only authorized users could submit reports and access their reporting history. It also strengthened data security by preventing unauthorized access to sensitive information.

**Figure 5**

**Home Dashboard**

![][image6]

Figure 5 presented the home dashboard of the mobile application. After successful login, users were redirected to the dashboard where they could easily access the major functions of the system.

The dashboard provided shortcuts for submitting reports, viewing ordinance information, checking report status, and managing the user's account. Its simple interface enabled users to navigate the application with minimal effort.

**Figure 6**

**Report Submission Module**

![][image7]

Figure 6 illustrated the report submission module of ORDINEX. This feature allowed residents to report municipal ordinance violations by entering the necessary information through a digital form.

Users were required to provide an attachment supporting images, and specify the location of the incident. These details helped municipal personnel verify reports and respond appropriately.

Compared with traditional reporting methods, the report submission module simplified the reporting process and minimized incomplete reports by organizing all required information within a single interface.

**Figure 7**

**Image Upload Feature**

![][image8]

Figure 7 presented the image upload feature integrated into the reporting module.

Users could attach photographs as supporting evidence before submitting their reports. Prior to uploading an image, the application displayed a data privacy notice reminding users that uploaded images might contain sensitive information. This feature promoted responsible handling of personal information while supporting compliance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012\.

The inclusion of image evidence enabled municipal personnel to validate reported violations more efficiently and reduced the possibility of inaccurate reports.

**Figure 8**

**Location Tagging**

![][image9]

Figure 8 illustrated the location tagging feature of the system.

The application records the location of the reported incident, allowing municipal personnel to accurately determine where the violation occurred. The inclusion of location data improved monitoring accuracy and assisted authorities in locating reported incidents more efficiently.

Location tagging also supported better documentation by associating each report with a specific geographical location.

**Figure 9**

**Report Status Monitoring**

![][image10]

Figure 9 presented the report status monitoring feature available to residents.

After submitting a report, users could monitor its progress through different status indicators such as Pending, Ongoing, and Completed. Any status updates made by municipal administrators were automatically synchronized through Firebase and immediately reflected within the mobile application.

This feature improves transparency by allowing users to monitor the progress of their submitted reports without repeatedly contacting the municipal office.

**Figure 10**

**Web-Based Administrator Dashboard**

![][image11]

Figure 10 showed the administrator dashboard developed using React.

The dashboard enabled authorized municipal personnel to view submitted reports, examine uploaded images, update report status, and communicate with reporting users. Reports were organized within a centralized database, making monitoring and management more efficient.

This administrative interface reduced manual record-keeping while improving report organization and response time.

**Figure 11**

**Firebase Database Structure**

![][image12]

Figure 11 illustrated the Firebase database used by the system.

Firebase stored user accounts, submitted reports, uploaded images, timestamps, report status, and other system information. Since Firebase supported real-time synchronization, any changes made by administrators were automatically reflected within the users' mobile application.

Cloud-based storage also improved data security, scalability, and system reliability.


Summary of the Developed System

The developed Mobile-Based Municipal Ordinance Reporting and Monitoring System successfully addressed the problems identified during the needs assessment. The integration of mobile reporting, image attachment, location tagging, cloud-based database management, and real-time report monitoring provided a more organized and efficient reporting process compared to traditional reporting methods.

The use of Flutter, React, and Firebase enabled the development of a responsive and reliable platform capable of supporting both residents and municipal personnel. By centralizing report management and improving communication between users and administrators, ORDINEX enhanced transparency, accessibility, and operational efficiency in managing municipal ordinance violations.

**Usability and Effectiveness of the Developed System Using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and User Feedback**

The third objective was to evaluate the usability and effectiveness of ORDINEX using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and user feedback. A total of 45 respondents evaluated the system: 20 residents, 10 barangay staff, 8 municipal staff, 2 national agency personnel, and 5 technical support personnel, as listed in Table 1 of Chapter II. 38 evaluated the mobile application and 7 evaluated the web-based administrator dashboard. Respondents answered a questionnaire that contained the ten SUS statements, four ORDINEX-specific statements, and two open-ended questions after using the system on October 8, 2026 at Bacnotan Municipal through Google Forms.

As shown in Table 11, the SUS scores of the 45 respondents ranged from 72.5 to 92.5, with a mean of 82.11 and a standard deviation of 5.22. All 45 respondents (100.0%) gave a score of 70 or above, which is the acceptable level in the rating scale of Chapter II.

Table 12 showed that the highest-rated item was item 3, “I thought ORDINEX was easy to use.” (adjusted score of 3.42 out of 4), while the lowest was item 1, “I think that I would like to use ORDINEX frequently.” (3.09). The negatively worded statements had low mean ratings (from 1.62 to 1.76), which meant respondents did not find the system complex, inconsistent, or cumbersome and did not feel that they needed technical support. All items were above the midpoint of the adjusted scale, which indicated good usability across the statements.

| Overall SUS Score | Adjective | Acceptability |

| 82.11 | Good | Acceptable |

*Adjective follows the rating scale in Chapter II (Poor below 60, Marginal 60–69, Acceptable 70–79, Good 80–89, Excellent 90–100). Grade follows the Sauro and Lewis (2016) curved grading scale.* 

As shown in Table 14, ORDINEX obtained an overall SUS score of 82.11, which was above the target score of 70 and fell in the Good range of the scale in Chapter II. This meant that users found the system acceptable and easy to learn and use. This result was consistent with Desmal et al. (2022), who concluded that usability was an important factor affecting user acceptance and satisfaction in mobile government services.

Table 15 showed an overall weighted mean of 4.27, interpreted as Strongly Agree. The highest-rated statement was that the status labels were clear (4.42), followed by the privacy notice before uploading an image (4.36) and the ease of submitting a report with text, photo, and location (4.33). The lowest was the promptness of status updates and notifications (3.98, Agree). These results show that the main functions named in the second objective worked as intended for the respondents, which supported the effectiveness of the system.

Table 16 showed that the most common positive comment was that the system made it easier to track submitted reports (13 respondents, 28.9%), followed by the organized layout and accessible main features (11, 24.4%). The most common suggestion was to add clearer guidance and tooltips for first-time users (12, 26.7%), followed by refining the layout for smaller mobile screens (10, 22.2%) and improving the map and location display (8, 17.8%). The feedback agreed with the SUS result: users liked the tracking and the layout, and their suggestions were refinements and not major problems. These results showed that the third objective of the study was achieved.

**CHAPTER IV**

**CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS**

This chapter presented the conclusions drawn from the results in Chapter III and the recommendations for future work. 

**Conclusions**

The needs survey of 40 respondents showed that privacy concern was the leading reason for not reporting ordinance violations (55.0%), that 44.1% of respondents with reporting experience were only sometimes informed of the outcome of their reports, and that reports were made mostly through verbal reports at the barangay hall (50.0%) and sent to several different offices. Therefore, the first objective of identifying the common challenges encountered by residents and local government units in reporting and managing municipal ordinance violations was achieved.

ORDINEX was developed as a mobile application with a web-based admin panel that allowed residents to submit reports using text, images, and location data and allowed municipal personnel to monitor and update the reports. Therefore, the second objective of designing and developing a mobile-based municipal ordinance reporting and monitoring system was achieved.

ORDINEX obtained an overall SUS score of 82.11, which was rated Good and above the target score of 70\. The ORDINEX-specific items were also rated Strongly Agree overall (4.27), with the status labels (4.42), the privacy notice before uploading an image (4.36), and the ease of submitting a report with text, photo, and location (4.33) rated highest, while the promptness of status updates and notifications (3.98) was rated Agree. Therefore, the third objective of evaluating the usability and effectiveness of the developed system was achieved.

**Recommendations**

Based on the results and limitations of the study, the following recommendations are given:

1\.    Future developers may add an offline mode that saves a report on the device and sends it when the connection returns, because 16 of 40 respondents (40.0%) described their internet access as unstable or limited.

2\.    Future developers may add an anonymous reporting option in which the identity of the reporter is visible only to authorized personnel, because privacy was the leading reason for not reporting (59.5%) and 17 respondents (42.5%) chose anonymous reporting as a useful feature.

3\.    Future developers may release ORDINEX on both Android and iOS, because all 40 respondents (100.0%) owned a smartphone, of whom 32 (80.0%) used Android and 8 (20.0%) used iPhone.

4\.    The municipality may set a target response time and use the status tracking and notification features for every report, because 15 of 34 respondents who had reported (44.1%) were informed of the outcome of their reports only sometimes.

5\.    Future developers may add a verification step for submitted reports, such as required photo evidence or account verification, because the accuracy of reports depended on the information given by users, as stated in the limitations in Chapter I.

6\.    Future researchers may evaluate ORDINEX with more respondents from more barangays of Bacnotan, La Union, because the system was tested only among selected respondents in specific areas.

Project Context

Traditionally, reporting municipal ordinance violations is done through manual methods such as verbal complaints, written reports, and even social media posts. However, these methods are often unorganized, difficult to monitor, and inefficient. As a result, delays in response and poor tracking of complaints commonly occur.

Local Government Units, or LGUs—especially at the barangay level—are responsible for maintaining public safety, order, and community welfare. Despite this responsibility, many LGUs still rely on these traditional reporting systems, which limit accessibility and create communication gaps between residents and local authorities.

In the Municipality of Bacnotan, La Union, these challenges are clearly observed. Residents often experience difficulty in submitting complaints quickly, while barangay and municipal officials struggle to organize, track, and respond to reports effectively. This situation highlights the need for a more efficient, accessible, and technology-driven solution.

Recent studies support the integration of digital technologies in local governance. For example, Cuevas et al. (2024) found that using geolocation and a Tagalog-based chatbot with natural language processing improves community engagement and service efficiency. Similarly, EACOMM Corporation (2023) emphasized that digital platforms and artificial intelligence can enhance public service delivery through faster communication and automation.

Additionally, Jakaria (2025) discussed the digital transformation in the Philippines, noting that while technology improves efficiency, proper system design and accessibility are essential for successful implementation. Supporting this, Mando (2022) developed a Barangay E-Complaint Management System that improved complaint handling through digitalization.

Further studies, such as Ormillo et al. (2026), introduced a web-based barangay management system that enhanced data management and operational efficiency. Engbino et al. (2022) also showed that integrating notification systems like SMS and email improves responsiveness and keeps stakeholders informed in real time.

Building on these findings, our study proposes a web-based municipal ordinance reporting and monitoring system with chatbot support. This system allows residents to submit reports in real time using their devices, while enabling local officials to efficiently monitor, verify, and respond to incidents.

The inclusion of a chatbot also provides users with instant access to ordinance-related information, increasing awareness and encouraging compliance within the community.

Overall, this project aims to bridge the communication gap between citizens and local government, while improving the efficiency, accessibility, and organization of ordinance reporting systems.

---

### **Gap of the Study** 

This study aims to address the following problems:

First, the lack of a centralized platform for reporting ordinance violations.  
 Second, poor documentation and tracking of submitted complaints.  
 Third, delayed response and inefficient communication between residents and authorities.  
 And lastly, the absence of a real-time monitoring system for reported incidents.

---

### **Objectives**

The  main objective of the  study  aimed to design and develop a web-based municipal ordinance reporting and monitoring system that improves the accessibility, efficiency, and organization of reporting ordinance violations in Bacnotan, La Union.

Specifically, it aims to:

* identify the common challenges encountered by residents and local government units in reporting and managing municipal ordinance violations;  
* To design and develop a web-based municipal ordinance reporting and monitoring system support that allows users to submit reports using text, images, and location data.  
* evaluate the usability and effectiveness of the developed system using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and user feedback from selected respondents.

---

### **System Overview**

BEE-Alert is a web-based application designed to streamline the reporting process.

Residents can submit complaints online, including details such as the type of violation, location, and supporting evidence like photos.

On the other hand, LGU administrators can review, verify, and respond to these reports through a centralized dashboard.

The system also allows monitoring of report status, ensuring transparency and accountability.

---

### **Key Features**

The system includes the following key features:

* User registration and login for residents and administrators  
* Online submission of ordinance violation reports  
* Image upload for supporting evidence  
* Real-time status tracking of reports  
* Admin dashboard for monitoring and managing complaints  
* Notification system for updates on report status

---

### **Methodology (Kanban \- if included)**

The development of the system followed a Kanban-based approach.

Tasks were organized into stages such as To Do, In Progress, and Completed, allowing continuous development and improvement.

This approach ensured flexibility, better task management, and efficient workflow throughout the project.

---

### **Significance of the Study**

This project benefits multiple stakeholders:

For residents, it provides a convenient and accessible way to report violations.  
 For the LGU, it improves efficiency in handling complaints and enhances decision-making.  
 For the community, it promotes transparency, accountability, and faster response to issues.

---

### **Conclusion**

In conclusion, BEE-Alert addresses the challenges of traditional reporting methods by providing a structured and efficient system.

It enhances communication, improves documentation, and ensures faster response to ordinance violations.

Through this system, we aim to contribute to a safer, more organized, and responsive municipality.

---

### **Closing**

That concludes our presentation.

Thank you, and we are now ready to answer your questions.

# **FINAL DEFENSE Q\&A (30 QUESTIONS)**

### **1\. What problem does your system address?**

**Answer:**  
The system addresses the lack of a centralized and structured platform for reporting municipal ordinance violations, which leads to unorganized reports, delayed responses, and inefficient communication between residents and authorities .

### **2\. Why are current reporting methods ineffective?**

**Answer:**  
They lack documentation and standardization. Verbal reports are not recorded, written reports are slow, and social media posts are unstructured and hard to track .

### **3\. What makes your system different from existing methods?**

**Answer:**  
It provides a centralized digital platform with structured reporting, real-time monitoring, and chatbot assistance, which improves efficiency and accessibility.

### **4\. Why did you choose Bacnotan, La Union?\***

**Answer:**  
Because the municipality experiences similar issues such as informal reporting and lack of a centralized system .

### **5\. Who are the target users of your system?**

**Answer:**  
Residents, municipal staff, (and technical support personnel).

### **6\. What is your general objective?**

**Answer:**  
To develop a web-based system that improves the accessibility and efficiency of reporting and monitoring ordinance violations .

### **7\. What are your specific objectives?**

**Answer:**  
To identify challenges, develop the system with reporting and chatbot features, and evaluate usability using feedback and SUS .

### **8\. Were your objectives achieved? \#**

**Answer:**  
Yes, the system was successfully developed and evaluated using user feedback and usability testing.

### **9\. Explain your conceptual framework.**

**Answer:**  
It follows the Input–Process–Output model: users input report data, the system processes and stores it, and outputs organized reports and notifications .

### **10\. What inputs are used in your system?**

**Answer:**  
Text descriptions, images, and GPS location .

### **11\. What processes occur in your system? (Jib)**

**Answer:**  
Data validation, storage in Firebase, real-time processing, and notification to authorities .

### **12\. What outputs does your system produce?**

**Answer:**  
Organized reports, real-time notifications, and accessible ordinance information.

### **13\. How does the chatbot help users? \#**

**Answer:**  
It answers user inquiries about ordinances.

### **14\. What happens after a report is submitted?**

**Answer:**  
The report is stored in Firebase with details like location and timestamp and is accessible to authorities for monitoring .

### **16\. Why did you choose Firebase?** 

**Answer:**  
Firebase offers real-time database capabilities, scalability, and secure cloud storage .

### **18\. Why did you choose Kanban methodology?**

**Answer:**  
Because it allows continuous development, flexibility, and efficient task management through visual workflows .

### **19\. What are the phases of your Kanban process?**

**Answer:**  
Requirements, Planning, Design, Development, Testing, Deployment & Continuous Improvement, and Review .

### **20\. How does Kanban improve your workflow?**

**Answer:**  
It organizes tasks into stages, helps track progress, and identifies bottlenecks for better efficiency .

### **21\. What research design did you use?**

**Answer:**  
A mixed-methods approach combining quantitative (surveys) and qualitative (interviews) data .

### **22\. How many respondents participated?**

**Answer:**  
30 \- 40  respondents, including residents, municipal staff, and technical support .

### **23\. How did you gather data?**

**Answer:**  
Through surveys, interviews, and system evaluation procedures .

### **24\. What is the System Usability Scale (SUS)?**

**Answer:**  
A standardized tool used to evaluate usability, scoring systems from 0 to 100 based on user feedback .

### **25\. What are the limitations of your system? \#**

**Answer:**  
Dependence on internet connectivity, reliance on user input accuracy, and limited testing scope .

### **26\. How do you ensure data privacy?**

**Answer:**  
By obtaining informed consent, ensuring confidentiality, and securely handling all collected data .

### **27\. Can your system handle false reports?**

**Answer:**  
Reports are subject to validation by authorities, but advanced detection like AI filtering is not yet implemented.

### **28\. What challenges did you encounter?**

**Answer:**  
Challenges included data collection, system testing, and ensuring usability for different types of users.

### **29\. What are the benefits of your system?**

**Answer:**  
Improved reporting efficiency, better communication, centralized data management, and increased public awareness.

### **30\. What future improvements do you recommend?**

**Answer:**  
AI-based detection, offline functionality, and integration with national government systems .

Here is a **clear, defense-ready answer** you can deliver confidently:

---

**Answer:**  
We chose to develop a **web-based application** because it provides **greater accessibility, flexibility, and ease of use** for both residents and municipal staff.

First, a web-based system can be accessed using any device with a browser—such as smartphones, laptops, or desktop computers—without requiring installation. This makes it more inclusive, especially for users with different types of devices.

Second, it allows **centralized management of data**, where all reports are stored and accessed in one system. This is important for monitoring and tracking ordinance violations efficiently.

Third, web-based systems are **easier to maintain and update**, since changes can be applied on the server side without requiring users to download updates.

Lastly, it supports **real-time data access**, especially with the use of cloud services like Firebase, allowing both users and administrators to view updates instantly.

Overall, a web-based approach ensures that the system is **accessible, scalable, and efficient**, which aligns with our goal of improving reporting and communication between residents and local government units.

---

If they ask a **follow-up (very common)** like *“why not mobile-only?”*, you can add:

👉  
A purely mobile application would require installation and may limit accessibility, while a web-based system can be accessed immediately through a browser, making it more practical for a wider range of users.

---

If you want, I can give you a **short version (pang one-sentence answer)** or a **more technical version (pang panelist na programmer)**.

A clean, **defense-ready answer** is:

---

**Answer:**  
Reliability does not depend solely on whether the system is web-based or mobile-based—it depends on how the system is **designed, developed, and maintained**.

However, in our case, a **web-based application is more reliable** for several reasons:

First, it ensures **centralized control and updates**. Any fixes or improvements can be applied on the server side immediately, so all users access the latest version without needing to update the app.

Second, it offers **wider accessibility**, since users can access it through any browser and device, reducing compatibility issues.

Third, it simplifies **maintenance and troubleshooting**, because issues can be managed in one place rather than across multiple installed applications.

On the other hand, mobile applications can be more reliable in **offline functionality and device-specific performance**, but they require installation, updates, and device compatibility management.

---

**Conclusion (important for defense):**  
In general, both can be reliable, but for our system—which focuses on accessibility, real-time reporting, and centralized monitoring—a **web-based application is more suitable and reliable for our use case**.

## **🎤 PROPOSAL DEFENSE PRESENTATION SCRIPT**

### **Slide 1: Title Slide**

Good day everyone.  
 We are presenting our capstone project entitled **“BEE-Alert: A Web-Based Municipal Ordinance Reporting and Monitoring System.”**

---

### **Slide 2: Project Context**

Our study focuses on improving how municipal ordinance violations are reported and managed.

Currently, reporting is done through manual methods such as verbal complaints, written reports, and social media messages. These methods are often unorganized, inefficient, and difficult to monitor, resulting in delayed responses from local authorities.

This highlights the need for a centralized and digital reporting system.

---

### **Slide 3: Gap of the Study**

The identified gaps in the current system include:

* No centralized reporting system  
* Reports are unorganized and undocumented  
* Delayed response from authorities  
* Limited public awareness of ordinances

These problems reduce the efficiency of local government services.

---

### **Slide 4: Review of Related Literature**

Several studies support the need for digital solutions in local governance.

Engbino et al. (2021) developed a web-based monitoring system with SMS and email notifications.  
 Asis et al. (2022) created a barangay e-complaint system to improve reporting.  
 Cuevas et al. (2024) integrated geolocation and chatbot technology for better community engagement.  
 Ormillo et al. (2026) introduced a web-based barangay management system for digital record-keeping.

These studies show that digital systems improve efficiency and communication.

---

### **Slide 5: General Objectives**

The main objective of this study is to develop a web-based system that makes reporting and monitoring municipal ordinance violations easier, faster, and more organized.

---

### **Slide 6: Conceptual Framework / System Architecture**

The system collects user inputs such as reports, images, and location data.

These inputs are processed through a centralized system that generates organized reports, notifications, and accessible ordinance information for both users and LGU officials.

---

### **Slide 7: Statement of Objectives**

Specifically, this study aims:

* To identify challenges in current reporting methods  
* To develop a web reporting system with chatbot support  
* To evaluate the system using usability testing

---

### **Slide 8: Purpose and Description**

The purpose of this study is to provide a structured and efficient digital platform for reporting ordinance violations.

The system benefits:

Residents – easier and faster reporting

LGUs – better monitoring and response

Community – improved awareness and compliance

Researchers and future developers – reference for future systems

---

### **Slide 9–10: Scope and Limitations**

The system is designed for Bacnotan, La Union.

It allows residents to report violations using text, images, and location data, and includes a chatbot for ordinance inquiries.

However, it requires internet access, depends on user-submitted data accuracy, and is tested only in selected areas of Bacnotan. It also does not include advanced AI detection features.

---

### **Slide 11: Technical Background**

The system is developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the interface, and Firebase for real-time database management.

It includes features such as reporting, image capture, location tracking, and a chatbot assistant.

These technologies improve communication, speed up response time, and enhance data management.

---

### **Slide 12: Population and Locale**

The study was conducted in Bacnotan, La Union.

The respondents include:

* 20–30 residents  
* 5 municipal staff  
* 5 technical support personnel

Total respondents range from 30 to 40 individuals.

---

### **Slide 13: Ethical Considerations**

* For our ethical considerations, the study strictly follows principles to protect the rights and data of all users.


* First, the system ensures data privacy and confidentiality in accordance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012\. All personal information collected is securely stored and accessible only to authorized personnel.


* Second, informed consent is obtained from all participants before collecting any data. Users are clearly informed about how their information will be used.


* The system also follows the principle of data minimization, meaning only necessary and relevant information is collected for reporting purposes.


* To further protect users, security measures such as controlled access and secure storage are implemented. User identities may also be protected through anonymity when necessary.


* Additionally, the system promotes ethical use by discouraging false reporting and misuse of the platform. Transparency and accountability are maintained in how reports are processed and handled.


* Users are also given the right to access, update, or request deletion of their personal data.


* Finally, the system is designed to ensure fairness and avoid any form of discrimination or bias.

---

### **Slide 14: Methodology (Kanban)**

The system development follows the Kanban methodology.

Tasks are organized into To Do, In Progress, Testing, and Done columns.

This approach helps track progress and allows continuous improvement throughout development.

---

### **Slide 15–21: Development Phases**

The system development follows several phases:

**Phase 1 – Requirements:**  
 Identified problems through surveys and interviews.

**Phase 2 – Planning:**  
 Organized tasks such as frontend, backend, API integration, UI design, and chatbot development.

**Phase 3 – Design:**  
 Created UI designs and system flow using Figma.

**Phase 4 – Development:**  
 Built the system using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Firebase.

**Phase 5 – Testing:**  
 Tested system functionality and usability, and fixed errors.

**Phase 6 – Deployment:**  
 Released the system to selected users and gathered feedback.

**Phase 7 – Review:**  
 Evaluated system performance and ensured objectives were met.

---

Good day everyone, respected panelists, and faculty members.

We are the researchers. I am **Glenn N. Rivera, Mark Allen C. Almodovar, Jibreel A. Quimson,  and Jan Alexis G. Roldan**, from the **Bachelor of Science in Information Technology program of LORMA Colleges**.

Today, we are honored to present our capstone project entitled:

**“BEE-Alert: A Web-Based Municipal Ordinance Reporting and Monitoring System with Integrated Chatbot Support.”**

Before we begin, we would like to dedicate this work to everyone who supported us throughout the completion of this study — especially our **parents, families, friends, classmates, professors, and adviser**, whose encouragement and guidance helped us finish this project successfully.
